blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 lays down foundational definitions and concepts regarding property law in India.
Key property transfer mechanisms include Sale, Mortgage, Charge, Lease, Exchange, and Gift.
Understanding the various types of mortgages is essential for competitive law and banking examinations.
The Registration Act, 1908 provides the legal framework for compulsory and optional registration of property transfer instruments.

cells: Act by which living person conveys property to one or more living persons; inter vivos transfer; does not apply to testamentary dispositions
Land, benefits to arise out of land, things attached to earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to earth
Two witnesses who see transferor execute or receive acknowledgement; essential for sale, mortgage, gift, charge, lease
Imputed knowledge — would have known with reasonable care and enquiry; includes registration as constructive notice
Transfer of property during pendency of suit — purchaser takes subject to outcome of suit
Transfer made to defraud creditors voidable at option of creditors
Person who takes possession in part performance of contract cannot be dispossessed; equitable doctrine

blocks.content: 6.2 Sale, Mortgage, Charge, Lease, Exchange, Gift

rows: Substantive rules governing transfer of immovable property (Sale, Mortgage, Lease, Gift, Exchange)
Procedural requirements for formal registration and recordation of property transfer documents

cells: Transfer of ownership for price; immovable property > Rs.100: by registered instrument; moveable property: delivery sufficient
Transfer of interest in specific immovable property as security for repayment of money or performance of obligation
Personal obligation + right to sell through court; no possession transferred; mortgage deed required
Mortgage by Deposit of Title Deeds (Equitable Mortgage)
Deposit of title deeds with lender with intent to create security; no registration needed; most common for bank loans
Absolute transfer to mortgagee; reconveyance on repayment; registered deed required
Possession and rents transferred to mortgagee till repayment; no personal covenant
Not any of the above; combination; depends on contract terms
Immovable property made security without transfer of any interest; not technically mortgage; enforceable by court sale only
Transfer of right to enjoy immovable property for time or in perpetuity; lessor and lessee; rent as consideration
Mutual transfer of ownership of things; neither can be money; if both money — sale
Voluntary transfer of ownership without consideration; must be accepted by donee; revocable if made in contemplation of death (donatio mortis causa)

items: Definitions and key distinctions between Sale, Mortgage, Charge, Lease, Exchange, and Gift are high-yield exam topics.
Classifications and specific essential features of different types of mortgages under TPA 1882 are regularly queried.
Questions often test the interaction between TPA 1882 and mandatory registration provisions under the Registration Act, 1908.
